title: Business systems as safe agent tools
subtitle: Agents acting on payments, email, social platforms and private APIs without holding a key, with every action attributed

stats.label: provider keys held by any agent; every credential stays server-side
function crates in the estate carry the tool generator's fingerprints
approves every grant an outside assistant receives, on the consent screen

lede: Agents that do real work against real services need credentials, and the moment one holds a credential there is a key in a transcript, actions nobody can attribute, and a crash window where a charge is doubled or lost. I built a governed gateway that exposes provider tools, each rebuilt from the provider's API, to managed agents, with credentials held server-side and identity derived from the authenticated caller, so no tool argument can claim to be someone else. Start with Agents with real tools and no keys.
quote: Attribution that might be silently dropped is worse than none.
evidence: Tool synthesis and governed API integration: payments, email and social-publishing provider APIs rebuilt as agent tools behind one gateway, with 0 provider keys held by any agent.
Exactly-once delivery and crash recovery: durable accounting around every provider call so a restart never repeats it, and vendor events returned signed to the team that caused them.
Attribution design for agent actions: a per-provider capability table that writes attribution into a vendor payload only where that operation was shown to round-trip it.
Sandboxed code generation for agents: a generator emitting 8 framework and 6 sandboxed files per tool, callable only after a human restart, with 7 of 14 function crates carrying its fingerprints.
OAuth 2.0 and identity architecture: an access plane where 1 person approves every grant an outside assistant receives, on the consent screen.
author: Corey James
